paper-collaborating-generative-review-mo.needs: Full text not obtained; only a single citing sentence available, so the depth of engagement with CTGAN cannot be verified beyond a passing citation.

paper-collaborative-intrusion-detection-.summary: This paper presents a collaborative intrusion detection system for UAV groups that detects both network attacks (blackhole, grayhole, flooding) and in-flight threats (GPS spoofing, jamming), combining supervised/unsupervised learning with federated learning to preserve privacy across vehicles. To address class imbalance in network attack data, the authors compare Random Oversampling, SMOTENC, and CTGAN as oversampling techniques, finding CTGAN outperforms the others and adopting it as the default method used to balance training data for both centralized and federated learning subsystems. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as the chosen data-balancing generator underpinning the final reported results.
paper-collaborative-intrusion-detection-.needs: Not explicit whether the SDV-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation was used; no constructor parameters or import statements given.

paper-converting-structured-point-cloud-.summary: This paper proposes T2pNet, a 3D-CNN model that maps traffic accident features into a higher-dimensional point cloud representation to reduce information loss compared to 2D-CNN dimensionality-reduction approaches, and shows it outperforms state-of-the-art models on accident severity prediction, especially for serious and fatal cases. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as one of several prior architectures proposed for structured data modeling, not used or evaluated in the study.
paper-converting-structured-point-cloud-.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed further or only listed in related work.

paper-driven-model-probabilistic-evaluat.summary: This paper develops a data-driven predictive model based on a tabular prior-data fitted network (TabPFN) to probabilistically evaluate heavy metal immobilization in municipal solid waste treated with geopolymer binders, aiming to support waste treatment assessment and risk evaluation. The evidence available (metadata only) shows it cites the original 2016 SDV paper, but with no citing sentence or abstract text to indicate how the reference is used.
paper-driven-model-probabilistic-evaluat.needs: Full text, abstract, and citing sentence were not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV is merely cited in a reference list or engaged with more substantively.

paper-difftab-improved-denoising-diffusi.summary: DiffTab is a proposed denoising diffusion probabilistic model for generating synthetic continuous tabular data describing acidic wastewater sulfidation processes, aimed at augmenting scarce process data for downstream modeling. The metadata shows the paper cites the CTGAN, TGAN, and vine-copula papers, likely as prior tabular-data-generation methods situated in related work or as baseline comparators. No full text or citing sentences were available, so whether CTGAN/TGAN/vine-copula were actually run as baselines or only cited cannot be confirmed from this evidence.
paper-difftab-improved-denoising-diffusi.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN/TGAN/vine-copula were run as experimental baselines (baseline_only) or merely cited in related work (citation_only). Marked unclear pending full-text verification.

paper-ensuring-privacy-synthetic-generat.summary: This study investigates the use of privacy-preserving synthetic data generation techniques for educational datasets, evaluating whether combining synthetic data with differential privacy mechanisms can better balance data utility and privacy protection than traditional anonymisation. It examines several synthetic data generation techniques' capability to resist privacy threats such as linkage attacks while preserving dataset utility. CTGAN is cited as one of the synthetic data generation techniques considered in this comparative investigation.
paper-ensuring-privacy-synthetic-generat.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package, reimplemented, or only cited alongside other generative techniques.

paper-industrial-synthesis-framework-fau.summary: This conference paper proposes a diffusion- and flow-based generative framework for synthesizing industrial process data to address privacy concerns and fault-sample scarcity in fault diagnosis, validated on the Tennessee Eastman benchmark. In its related-work discussion of generative models for data privacy protection, it briefly describes prior work by Xu et al. proposing CTGAN and TVAE to generate synthetic credit card transaction records, without running either model. CTGAN and TVAE are cited only as prior tabular data-synthesis methods the authors' diffusion/flow approach is positioned against.
paper-industrial-synthesis-framework-fau.needs: Industry classification is approximate; Tennessee Eastman is a chemical-process fault diagnosis benchmark, could alternatively be tagged chemicals_materials rather than manufacturing.

paper-machine-learning-prediction-cognit.summary: This study analyzes 55 blood biomarkers in 39 SuperAgers versus 42 typical agers, using feature selection and machine learning to identify biomarkers predictive of superior cognitive function, and applies SHAP for interpretability. To address a small sample size, the authors augment their tabular data using GReaT, an LLM-based tabular data generator, which they explicitly contrast with CTGAN as an alternative approach. CTGAN is cited only in passing as the conventional GAN-based method for table data augmentation that the authors chose not to use.

paper-meta-heuristic-intrusion-detection.summary: This paper introduces an in-house intrusion detection dataset built from a controlled network testbed and evaluates several machine-learning classifiers alongside a proposed hybrid Slime Mould Optimization plus Decision Tree model for attack classification, reporting 94.44% accuracy. To address class imbalance in the collected attack dataset, CTGAN is applied to generate oversampled minority-class attack samples before classifier training.
paper-meta-heuristic-intrusion-detection.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm how or whether CTGAN is actually engaged with beyond a citation.

paper-spatially-adaptive-sub-sub-2025.summary: This paper proposes using Sparse Variational Gaussian Processes (SVGP) to estimate PM2.5 pollution levels in regions with sparse ground-sensor networks, exploiting the spatial adaptability of optimized inducing points to fill data gaps, validated on sensor data from Lima, Peru. The authors briefly suggest that inducing points could be combined with a generative architecture to further synthesize data reducing spatial irregularities, citing CTGAN as that generative architecture. CTGAN is only named in passing as a possible companion generative model and is not implemented or evaluated in the reported experiments.
paper-spatially-adaptive-sub-sub-2025.needs: No experiment or implementation involving CTGAN appears in the full text; the citation is a forward-looking suggestion only.

paper-synthetic-tabular-generation-horiz.summary: This paper simulates horizontal federated learning scenarios for synthetic tabular data generation in acute myeloid leukemia, comparing a nonfederated baseline against federated setups with varying node counts and data distributions using two generative models, CTGAN and FedTabDiff, evaluated on fidelity and privacy trade-offs. The authors report that federating the generative models degrades data fidelity relative to the centralized baseline while privacy levels are preserved, with the deterioration largely stable across node counts. CTGAN, run using the Synthetic Data Vault's implementation (v0.18.0) with default parameters, is one of the two generative models whose federated training and evaluation form the entire empirical programme, though the authors note modifications were needed to adapt it to the federated setting.
paper-synthetic-tabular-generation-horiz.needs: Unclear whether the 'modifications' for federated use altered CTGAN's internal training loop/architecture (which would push toward derivative_work) or only its orchestration across nodes; evidence text does not specify further.

paper-synthetic-external-control-arms-20.summary: This paper proposes a reversible data-generalization procedure to reduce cardinality before synthesizing scarce, high-cardinality clinical trial data, then reverses it post-synthesis, and tests six generator algorithms (Dummy, CTGAN, Survival CTGAN, DP-GAN, PATEGAN, PrivBayes, Uniform) implemented via the synthcity package against utility and privacy metrics using Norwegian cancer registry data as an external control arm. PrivBayes, CTGAN and PATEGAN emerged as the preferred generators for producing synthetic control-arm data with acceptable fidelity and privacy. CTGAN, cited to the SDV-family NeurIPS 2019 paper, is run as one of several benchmarked generators (via synthcity, not the sdv-dev package) rather than as the paper's own contribution.
paper-synthetic-external-control-arms-20.needs: CTGAN here is invoked through the synthcity package rather than sdv-dev, so no SDV code itself runs; treated as inherited rather than api_user.

paper-big-architecture-digital-twin-2024.summary: This paper proposes a Big Data architecture for building Digital Twin models of railway switch points and signals from heterogeneous sensor data, aimed at supporting predictive maintenance and simulation in the railway industry. The authors generate synthetic railway signal data using several deep generative models and compare them using FID, Precision, Recall, and Coverage metrics. CTGAN is run as one of several generative models evaluated, performing well on coverage alongside CWGAN-GP but being surpassed overall by TimeGAN.

paper-systematic-review-synthetic-genera.summary: This is a systematic literature review surveying generative-AI techniques for synthetic data generation -- rule-based systems, GANs, VAEs, and LLM-based approaches -- across domains such as healthcare and finance, identifying limitations and future research directions. It discusses CTGAN in detail as prior literature, describing its mode-specific normalization, conditional generator, and training-by-sampling strategy for handling imbalanced tabular data, without running any experiments itself. CTGAN's design is only described and cited as prior art, never executed by the authors.

paper-empirical-utility-disclosure-risk-.summary: This paper presents an in-depth empirical study of utility and disclosure risk metrics across classical and deep-learning tabular data synthesis models (Gaussian Copula, CART, CTGAN, and TVAE), evaluated on multiple datasets including Census and Ethereum data. It finds trade-offs between continuous-attribute proportion, synthetic data volume, and both utility and disclosure risk, and shows that a widely-used disclosure metric (TCAP) fails to detect certain vulnerable outlier records. Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE synthesizers, run with library-style hyperparameters, are evaluated side by side as the paper's primary experimental subjects for utility and privacy-risk comparison.
paper-empirical-utility-disclosure-risk-.needs: Unclear whether GC/CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv package directly or via the standalone ctgan package; both are plausible given the described hyperparameters.

paper-application-deep-learning-models-2.summary: This paper presents a framework for generating production-like software test data using deep-learning language models (char-RNN, VAE, GAN), evaluated on a case study of the Norwegian National Population Registry and deployed in a real test environment. In its related-work discussion of relational database synthesis, it describes SDV as 'a general end-to-end synthetic data generator... to synthesize complete tables of a relational database,' contrasting it with the authors' own event-based, language-modeling approach. SDV is only cited and described, not run in the experiments.

paper-bankgan-generative-model-synthetic.summary: BankGAN is a generative model for synthesizing bank transaction sequences with non-uniform date patterns, combining CTGAN's architecture with Banksformer's date-handling mechanism and a sequence conditional vector to represent categorical, continuous, and date-related variables. The authors report it outperforms RNN- and transformer-based baselines in statistical resemblance and periodic-pattern replication while preserving privacy without degrading quality. BankGAN maintains CTGAN's generator/discriminator architecture, training-by-sampling technique, and mode-specific normalization, extending its conditional vector design to build a new sequence-aware synthesizer.
paper-bankgan-generative-model-synthetic.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliations and venue could not be confirmed from abstract/metadata alone.

paper-crtgan-controllable-road-network-2.summary: This paper proposes CRTGAN, a transformer-based GAN pipeline for generating road network graphs with controllable spatial and topological properties, including a differentiable image-to-graph extractor for end-to-end training. It is evaluated on road network datasets and achieves strong performance on a traffic convenience metric. The CTGAN paper is cited only in passing as an example of 'pre-generation control,' where a control signal is input to the model before data generation, without any use of the CTGAN library or model.
paper-crtgan-controllable-road-network-2.needs: CTGAN is cited only as an example of a 'pre-generation control' mechanism analogous to conditional generation; no CTGAN code, model, or experiment is used in this road-network paper.

paper-logistics-supply-chain-mcdm-2024.summary: Ranks five logistics supply chain factors for global trade using fuzzy AHP with triangular fuzzy numbers and a PROMETHEE-style outranking step, driven by pairwise judgements elicited from industry practitioners and researchers, and concludes that promoting export dominates the alternatives. SDV enters only as a cited name: both the Patki thesis and the Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni paper sit in the bibliography and the phrase augmenting synthetic data vault appears in the method, but no synthesizer is run and no synthetic data is characterised anywhere in the paper.
paper-logistics-supply-chain-mcdm-2024.needs: The SDV citations in this paper appear misapplied rather than substantive: Patki (2016) is cited inline for definitional claims about logistics and supply chain management, and the one methodological mention of the synthetic data vault carries citations to two unrelated works. Recorded citation_only importance 1 on the ground that the SDV papers are genuinely in the bibliography. Saman may prefer to drop the entry entirely, as three papers were dropped from the IEEE lane for having no real SDV content

paper-deep-learning-assisted-cancer-2024.summary: This paper proposes WT-GAN, a Wasserstein Tabular GAN-based data augmentation method for microarray gene expression cancer data, combined with correlation-based feature selection and deep FNN/ML classifiers, achieving over 97% classification accuracy on augmented data. The paper's own synthesizer, not an SDV library, generates the synthetic gene expression samples. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is cited only for the mutual-information similarity test used to validate synthetic data quality, with no SDV code run.
paper-deep-learning-assisted-cancer-2024.needs: The paper's own WT-GAN model may be inspired by TGAN's tabular GAN design but the full text shows no SDV code, package, or architecture description used -- treated as citation_only.

paper-enhancing-tabular-gan-fairness-202.summary: This ICMLA 2024 paper addresses fairness in GAN-based synthetic tabular data generation by proposing an intersectional fairness framework that identifies problematic sensitive-feature combinations via explainability techniques and incorporates an intersectional demographic parity constraint into GAN training. The authors modify the loss functions of two state-of-the-art tabular GANs, TabFairGAN and CTGAN, and evaluate the resulting fairness/accuracy trade-offs on the Adult and Diabetes datasets. CTGAN's own generator/critic loss is directly modified to add the fairness constraint, making CTGAN's conditional generator architecture one of the two synthesizers whose training objective is extended and empirically evaluated throughout the paper.
paper-enhancing-tabular-gan-fairness-202.needs: Unclear whether the CTGAN implementation used is the sdv-dev package modified, or a reimplementation from scratch; the paper describes modifying the loss function but does not name the software package, so derivative_work vs. port is a judgment call.

paper-shallows-depths-unveiling-hybrid-2.summary: This article proposes a hybrid synthetic-data generation approach combining shallow interpolation-based methods with deep generative models to address class imbalance and privacy constraints in small, imbalanced datasets used for machine learning. It frames its contribution against prior tabular data synthesis approaches, describing how earlier LSTM/GMM-based tabular generators were superseded by CTGAN, which the authors discuss for replacing conventional GAN losses and using fully-connected generator/discriminator layers. CTGAN (and the earlier TGAN) are cited and described as prior art the authors' own approach departs from, rather than being run in the reported experiments.
paper-shallows-depths-unveiling-hybrid-2.needs: Full text not available; unable to confirm whether CTGAN was actually run as part of the hybrid model's experiments or only discussed in related work. Authors' affiliations not stated in available evidence.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-im.summary: This paper proposes a deep learning intrusion detection system for software-defined networks that uses a GAN-based technique to generate synthetic minority-class samples, addressing severe class imbalance in IDS datasets, and combines chi-square feature selection with several ML classifiers (Naive Bayes, Extra Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost) for evaluation. The work cites the CTGAN paper as the basis for its synthetic data generation approach for balancing intrusion detection data. It is unclear from the available evidence whether the SDV-distributed CTGAN implementation was actually run or whether the authors built their own GAN inspired by it.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-im.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract only refers generically to 'GAN' without naming CTGAN explicitly, so it is unclear whether the SDV/CTGAN implementation was actually run (api_user) or merely cited as prior art for a custom GAN (citation_only).

paper-improving-admissions-forecasting-g.summary: This paper proposes a generative-AI approach based on DGAN (Doppelganger-style GAN) to forecast emergency department (ED) admissions from sequential/time-series hospital data. It cites the DeepEcho sequential synthesizer paper (PAR) from the SDV family, likely as related prior work on generating sequential synthetic data, but the full text was not available to confirm whether PAR was run or only referenced.
paper-improving-admissions-forecasting-g.needs: Full text needed to confirm whether PAR/DeepEcho was run as a baseline or only cited; role of DGAN vs SDV components unclear from metadata alone.

paper-systematic-review-generative-model.summary: A systematic review of synthetic tabular data generation methods and utility evaluation metrics, surveying Bayesian networks, CART-based methods, and GAN/VAE approaches across the literature and proposing a utility evaluation tool of the authors' own. As part of their own empirical benchmark the authors run CTGAN directly against synthpop (CART) and DataSynthesizer (BN) across 18 datasets to compare utility and privacy scores. CTGAN, the SDV-family GAN model, is run as one of three generative models in the authors' own benchmark, its performance and privacy/utility trade-offs reported and discussed alongside SDMetrics and the Synthetic Data Vault's GaussianCopula noted elsewhere only as prior literature.
paper-systematic-review-generative-model.needs: Other SDV mentions (Copula/Synthetic Data Vault, SDMetrics) appear only as citations describing surveyed prior work or available tools, not run by the authors; only CTGAN is actually executed in this paper's own benchmark.

paper-taxonomy-prompt-engineering-genera.summary: This paper presents a taxonomy-based prompt engineering approach to generate synthetic patient portal messages related to drug use, likely using large language models rather than tabular synthesis methods. It appears to address text-based synthetic data generation for healthcare NLP applications. The paper cites the CTGAN paper, likely as related prior work on synthetic data generation methods, without evidence of running it.
paper-taxonomy-prompt-engineering-genera.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed, run, or merely listed among synthetic data generation citations. Title suggests text-based (LLM) synthetic message generation, making CTGAN's role likely peripheral, but this cannot be verified from metadata alone.

paper-usability-synthetic-dataset-decisi.summary: Asks whether a synthetic dataset is actually usable for clinical decision support rather than merely statistically plausible, and answers it on electronic health records with three yardsticks at once: accuracy of models trained on it (random forest drops 0.9444 to 0.8704), similarity to the original (0.9044) and privacy (0.9988 and 0.6507 under two threat models), with no synthetic row matching a real one. CTGAN is the sole generator and the method is judged usable, but no library is named, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.
paper-usability-synthetic-dataset-decisi.needs: IEEE Xplore is paywalled to automated fetches; the similarity and privacy scores resemble SDMetrics output but the implementation is unconfirmed.

paper-accelerated-alloy-discovery-synthe.summary: This materials-science article proposes a workflow that combines synthetic data generation with data-mining techniques to accelerate the discovery of new metal alloys. No abstract or full text was available to establish which synthetic-data method or tool is used, only that the metadata indicates a citation to an SDV-family paper. The specific SDV component and how it is used could not be determined from the available evidence.

paper-addressing-bottleneck-medical-deep.summary: This paper presents a human-in-the-loop machine learning pipeline that combines data augmentation with active and interactive learning to address data scarcity in a neural-network model for pancreatic cancer treatment decisions. Synthetic patient cases are generated by a CTGAN, and human experts act as an additional discriminatory layer, converting rejected synthetic cases into new constraints that are fed back into the generator across training iterations. The authors explicitly used the CTGAN implementation from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) project because it supports defining constraints between columns to prohibit implausible combinations, running SDV's CTGAN as the core generator for their entire augmentation and human-feedback loop.

paper-explanatory-predictive-model-covid.summary: This study measures plasma levels of 48 cytokines in 87 COVID-19 patients and trains machine learning and deep learning classifiers to predict disease severity, using SHAP and LIME to interpret which cytokines (e.g., VEGF-A, MIP-1b, IL-17) drive severity classification. The paper mentions using ML/DL to complete missing data and generate synthetic data to fill gaps, but the full text search confirms CTGAN is never invoked in the pipeline. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it was run.

paper-generating-synthetic-population-tr.summary: This paper proposes a Transformer-based generative model for synthesizing individual-level demographic microsimulation populations, generating both numerical and categorical attributes while preserving population heterogeneity and diversity. The authors compare their model against a baseline CTGAN model on real census microdata, evaluating fit via WMAPE and diversity metrics, finding their Transformer approach generally outperforms CTGAN. CTGAN, run via the SDV library, is used as the comparison baseline synthesizer throughout the empirical evaluation.
paper-generating-synthetic-population-tr.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract does not mention CTGAN directly, so its exact role (baseline vs. one of several comparisons) and result placement relative to the proposed Transformer model are unconfirmed.

paper-mtgan-2023.summary: Proposes MTGAN for generating time-series electronic health records, targeting the uncommon diseases existing EHR generators under-represent. CTGAN is both a baseline and the source of the mechanism: the smooth conditional matrix broadcasts CTGAN's conditional vector across a visit sequence, and real-sample selection follows CTGAN's training-by-sampling.

paper-pre-trained-tabular-transformer-20.summary: This conference paper applies TabPFN, a pre-trained tabular Transformer, to Radiomics data from three clinical imaging datasets (ultrasound kidney tumor classification, CT lung cancer EGFR mutation prediction, and MRI brain metastases treatment response), showing it outperforms other tabular ML methods and evaluating its clinical translation potential. It cites CTGAN only as part of a one-sentence roadmap of tabular data modeling techniques ('using GAN [17]') without further discussion or experimentation.
paper-pre-trained-tabular-transformer-20.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract and citing sentence confirm CTGAN is only cited as prior art, not used in experiments.

paper-privlava-synthesizing-relational-f.summary: This paper proposes PrivLava, the first method for synthesizing relational data with foreign keys under differential privacy, using graphical models with latent variables to capture inter-relational correlations across a directed acyclic graph of foreign-key references. Experiments on census data and TPC-H show it outperforms prior single-relation and multi-relation baselines on aggregate query accuracy. CTGAN is cited only in passing, grouped with other GAN-based approaches, as prior work whose performance is noted to be inferior to graphical-model methods per another cited study.

paper-privacy-assessment-synthetic-patie.summary: This paper quantifies the privacy gain of synthetic patient data generated by two differentially private generative models, MST and PrivBayes, trained on real anonymized UK primary-care patient data from CPRD Aurum. Using the TAPAS toolbox, the authors evaluate membership and attribute inference attacks under black-box threat models, finding PrivBayes more robust than MST though both remain vulnerable for some outlier records. CTGAN is only mentioned in a list of generators found in the literature and is not used to generate or evaluate any of the paper's synthetic data.
paper-privacy-assessment-synthetic-patie.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm how or where CTGAN is mentioned (likely related work citation) since it is absent from the abstract's described experiments.

paper-privacy-preserving-approximate-que.summary: This conference paper integrates several differentially private generative models (PATE-CTGAN, DP-CTGAN, DP-GAN) with an approximate query processing (AQP) engine, evaluating synthetic data quality and query relative error on a Parkinson's disease dataset. Non-private CTGAN is trained and used as a baseline against which the DP variants are compared, and the authors' quality assessment relies on the SDMetrics Quality Report tool to score column shapes and pair trends. CTGAN thus serves as the non-private comparison baseline while SDMetrics is run directly as the evaluation library underpinning the paper's quality metrics.
paper-privacy-preserving-approximate-que.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev ctgan package directly or a separate implementation; SDMetrics use is explicit and directly linked to the sdv-dev GitHub repo.

paper-production-quality-prediction-mult.summary: This paper proposes a multi-task joint deep learning framework for predicting production quality across multistage manufacturing systems, aiming to improve prediction accuracy by jointly learning related quality tasks. The evidence available does not describe the experimental pipeline or datasets in detail. The work cites the CTGAN paper, but how it uses CTGAN cannot be determined from the metadata alone.
paper-production-quality-prediction-mult.needs: Full text and citing sentence not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run for data augmentation or merely cited in passing.

paper-addressing-training-scarcity-chall.summary: A survey and proposed framework addressing the scarcity of training data for AI-driven radio access network (RAN) automation, taxonomizing techniques such as interpolation, domain-knowledge methods, GANs, transfer learning, autoencoders, few-shot learning, and simulators/testbeds, and proposing new approaches like matrix completion. CTGAN and TGAN are named only in a bibliographic list of works that apply GANs to tabular data outside the cellular network domain, with no experiments or engagement in this survey. SDV's CTGAN and TGAN are cited only, not run or discussed in any depth.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-sp.summary: A comprehensive survey of GAN architectures and evaluation practices applied to spatio-temporal data, covering applications such as trajectory prediction, event generation, and time-series imputation, and outlining future research directions. The survey catalogs generative and qualitative evaluation methods used across the reviewed literature. CTGAN appears only in the reference list among a long set of evaluation-metric and GAN citations, with no discussion or use in the body text.

paper-challenges-opportunities-generativ.summary: This paper compares Markov Chain Monte Carlo, GAN, and VAE-based generative methods for producing synthetic network intrusion detection data, aiming to address the scarcity of labeled cyber attack datasets for training ML-based IDS. The authors fit MCMC, CTGAN, and TVAE models on the same 10,000-record NSL-KDD sample and score the synthetic outputs with an inverted Kolmogorov-Smirnov D statistic, finding CTGAN performs best. Both CTGAN and TVAE are run directly via the 'synthetic data vault Python package' with default settings as two of the three generative methods evaluated, and the KS D-statistic scoring approach is attributed to the original SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016).
paper-challenges-opportunities-generativ.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether TVAE was actually run in experiments or only mentioned as an available SDV implementation, and whether CTGAN was invoked via the sdv library or the standalone ctgan package. Author affiliations not stated in available evidence.

paper-detecting-cognitive-impairment-sta.summary: This paper develops a machine learning pipeline that uses keystroke dynamics and smartwatch-derived physical activity data to classify cognitive impairment severity (normal, mild, moderate, severe) among older adults, with a Gradient Boosting Machine achieving over 94% accuracy. To address class imbalance in their collected dataset, the authors augment 10% of the data using the Conditional Tabular GAN. CTGAN is run directly as a data augmentation tool to synthesize minority-class tabular samples before classifier training.
paper-detecting-cognitive-impairment-sta.needs: Affiliation names for the two numbered institutions were not present in the extracted first page text, only superscript markers '1' and '2'.

paper-imbalanced-sample-generation-evalu.summary: This conference paper proposes a controllable sample generation framework for power system transient stability assessment, addressing insufficient and imbalanced training samples by modeling transient stability samples as tabular data, applying Gaussian mixture model normalization, and using a multi-condition vector to control generation. The authors design their own generator and discriminator with fully connected layers rather than importing a library, and introduce three evaluation metrics to assess sample quality and downstream assessment performance. The work adopts CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generation design, reimplemented from scratch as the paper's own network rather than run via the SDV library.
paper-imbalanced-sample-generation-evalu.needs: Whether authors used the sdv-dev CTGAN package underneath their custom layers is not stated; text describes building generator/discriminator layers themselves, suggesting reimplementation (port) rather than api_user.

paper-integrated-modelling-mapping-spati.summary: This is an environmental-science study that develops an integrated modelling framework -- combining feature selection (LOFO), deep learning models (gcForest, Bi-LSTM), game theory and a Gaussian copula-based multivariate model -- to map dust-emission susceptibility across Central Asia. The paper identifies key environmental drivers (bulk density, precipitation, coarse fragment content) and produces spatial susceptibility maps for the region. It cites SDV-family papers (the SDV framework paper and the TGAN paper) in its background/related-work discussion of generative or copula-based modelling, without evidence that any SDV-family software was actually run.
paper-integrated-modelling-mapping-spati.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the 'Gaussian copula-based multivariate model' is linked to SDV's GaussianCopula implementation or is an independent statistical construction, nor how/why TGAN is cited in this environmental-science paper.

paper-poster-abstract-class-balancing-20.summary: A poster abstract proposing the use of GANs to address class imbalance in human comfort datasets, likely used in building science or occupant comfort research. No abstract or full text was available to describe the method or experiments in detail. The work cites the TGAN (2018) paper, apparently as related prior work on tabular data generation.
paper-poster-abstract-class-balancing-20.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is run experimentally or merely cited, nor the authors' institutional affiliation beyond the NUS ScholarBank repository link.

paper-super-resolution-generative-advers.summary: This paper proposes using super-resolution GANs (SRGAN) to upsample low-resolution wheat crop images before training a CNN to classify wheat yellow (stripe) rust, showing improved detection accuracy versus using low-resolution images directly. The work is entirely about image super-resolution and disease classification, with no tabular data synthesis involved. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only in passing, in a background sentence noting that GANs have also been applied to tabular data synthesis, as one of two example references.

paper-testing-object-detection-autonomou.summary: This paper proposes an automatic method for testing DNN-based object detection in autonomous driving systems by synthesizing natural-looking images via 3D reconstruction of vehicles inserted into real driving photos, evaluated on 500 Apollo dataset photos. The approach uses vanishing point estimation and heuristic-based image insertion rather than any generative model. The original SDV paper is cited once in passing to support the general claim that artificial data can partially replace real data, with no SDV component or method actually used.
paper-testing-object-detection-autonomou.needs: Full text not available; the single citing sentence suggests only a generic reference to synthetic data, not use of any SDV component.

paper-electricity-theft-detection-machin.summary: This conference paper proposes an electricity theft detection model combining LSTM feature extraction with RUSBoost classification to address data imbalance and detection accuracy in smart grid consumption data, comparing results against SVM and Logistic Regression baselines. CTGAN is only listed in the reference list and does not appear anywhere in the body text describing the method or experiments.
paper-electricity-theft-detection-machin.needs: Full text or citing sentence needed to determine whether CTGAN was run for data augmentation/class imbalance in theft detection or merely cited in related work.

paper-generation-evaluation-privacy-pres.summary: This paper presents a pipeline for generating and evaluating privacy-preserving synthetic health data, addressing how to produce realistic patient records while protecting individual privacy. The authors describe adapting data transformation strategies used in the Synthetic Data Vault for their own preprocessing pipeline. SDV's data transformation approach is cited and adapted rather than run directly as a library component.
paper-generation-evaluation-privacy-pres.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether SDV code was actually run or only its transformation design was reimplemented in the authors' own pipeline.

preprint-geometry-aware-tabular-diffusio.summary: This paper introduces Geometry-Aware Tabular Diffusion (GATD), a tabular diffusion model that augments denoisers with explicit pairwise angle and length features as auxiliary supervision, improving distributional fidelity and downstream utility across MLP, GNN, and Transformer backbones while using far fewer parameters than prior state-of-the-art. The authors evaluate synthetic data quality on ten benchmark datasets using Shape and Trend metrics computed via SDMetrics, and separately discuss CTGAN/TVAE as an MLP-backbone prior method that TabDiff outperformed. SDMetrics (mis-cited to the original SDV paper) supplies the ColumnShapeSimilarity and ColumnPairTrendsSimilarity metrics that anchor the paper's headline evaluation results, while CTGAN is only referenced in a literature comparison, not run.
preprint-geometry-aware-tabular-diffusio.needs: CTGAN/TVAE mention is a citation to prior literature (via TabDiff's reported comparison), not run by this paper itself; included in sdv_component as a mis-cited/citation-only mention.

preprint-hierarchical-synthetic-tabular-.summary: This paper proposes H-TDBU, a hybrid top-down/bottom-up synthetic tabular data generation framework that combines rule-based logical constraints with lightweight statistical generators to improve semantic consistency and rare-event coverage on weak multimodal financial benchmarks. The authors evaluate their framework against several baselines including tree-based methods, a Gaussian copula, and neural generators. CTGAN and TVAE from SDV are explicitly run as 'SDV neural baselines' for comparison against the proposed hierarchical framework.

preprint-improving-credit-card-fraud-202.summary: This preprint proposes a transformer-enhanced GAN-based oversampling method aimed at mitigating class imbalance in credit card fraud detection datasets, presumably comparing its synthetic minority samples against existing generative oversampling approaches. Only metadata is available, so the exact experimental design and role of SDV-family work cannot be confirmed. The paper cites CTGAN (NeurIPS 2019) and the original SDV (DSAA 2016) papers, apparently as related prior generative approaches to tabular data synthesis for oversampling.
preprint-improving-credit-card-fraud-202.needs: Full text not available; cannot determine whether CTGAN is run as a baseline, adapted into the transformer-enhanced GAN, or merely cited as related work. Integration and importance are provisional.

paper-ctgan-palliative-care-2026.summary: Estimates whether palliative care buffers a surviving spouse against depression, a question that SHARE panel data cannot answer directly because the treated cohort is too small after attrition, by augmenting both arms with synthetic longitudinal trajectories and then applying a matched difference-in-differences estimator. CTGAN is the generator that augmentation runs on, selected over TVAE and a transformer VAE and used unmodified inside a purpose-built pipeline that flattens each survivor's waves into one wide vector, resamples a real baseline skeleton for every synthetic unit and conditions the trajectory on it, so the paper's causal estimates rest on CTGAN output.

paper-spine-registry-synthetic-2026.summary: Releases synthetic data from a multicentre spine surgery registry, where institutional governance rather than technical difficulty is what blocks sharing. A GaussianCopula model is trained on 52 structured variables, so SDV is the mechanism by which a governed clinical registry becomes distributable.

preprint-cross-flow-correlations-survive.summary: This paper investigates privacy leakage in synthetic network traffic generators (SynNetGens), showing that cross-flow behavioral correlations preserved in synthesis can expose source-level membership even when packet- or flow-level differential privacy is applied. The authors introduce TraceBleed, a source-level membership inference attack evaluated against six SynNetGens across five datasets, and propose a public privacy-fidelity leaderboard. CTGAN's NeurIPS 2019 paper is cited among a list of related generative-synthesis works but is not directly run or engaged with in the visible evidence.
preprint-cross-flow-correlations-survive.needs: The single extracted passage does not show CTGAN being run or discussed directly; unclear whether CTGAN underlies one of the six evaluated SynNetGens or is purely a background citation.

preprint-privacy-preserving-diffusion-mo.summary: This paper introduces DP-FinDiff, a differentially private diffusion model for synthesizing mixed-type tabular data, using embedding-based categorical representations plus an adaptive timestep sampler and feature-aggregated loss to reduce DP-training bias and improve utility on financial and medical datasets. The authors evaluate it against re-implemented differentially private versions of TVAE, CTGAN, and TabDDPM rather than the original models. CTGAN and TVAE, from the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are reimplemented with DP-SGD training and run as baseline comparators, not executed via the sdv-dev library itself.
preprint-privacy-preserving-diffusion-mo.needs: Unclear whether the CTGAN/TVAE reimplementation used any sdv-dev source code as a starting point versus building purely from the architecture description in Xu et al. 2019; treated as an authors' own reimplementation (port) since DP-SGD was integrated into the training loop.

paper-snn-fraud-hyperheuristic-2025.summary: Combines a cortical spiking network with population coding and a reinforcement-guided hyper-heuristic search over its hyperparameters for detecting fraudulent bank account applications, targeting accuracy alongside group fairness and explainability, and evaluates it on the six bias variants of the Bank Account Fraud suite against gradient-boosted and prior spiking baselines under a reward that trades predictive equality against parameter count. CTGAN is the generator that produced the benchmark this work runs on: the paper records that the Bank Account Fraud suite was synthesized with it to preserve applicant anonymity, and states explicitly that CTGAN belongs to the dataset's creation and not to its own training pipeline.
paper-snn-fraud-hyperheuristic-2025.needs: no convention covers this shape. The paper never runs CTGAN, yet every row it trains and evaluates on is CTGAN output, produced by the third-party Bank Account Fraud dataset authors. Recorded citation_only importance 2 as the conservative reading of the existing scale (CTGAN described, not run). The alternative is `inherited`, whose definition - SDV arrived inside a vendored third party rather than by a decision to embed it, and the intermediary is usually an index entry in its own right - fits closely if it is read to cover a third-party dataset as well as a vendored library, with the BAF suite as the intermediary entry. Importance would then plausibly be 3 rather than 2, since the paper's entire empirical substrate is CTGAN output. Needs a ruling before other dataset-inheritance cases are judged.

preprint-synthetic-child-adolescent-ment.summary: This preprint describes the use of synthetic data derived from a large-scale EMR-based cohort of Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) patients in Stavanger, Norway, to enable confidential yet detailed analysis for mental-health resource planning. The authors argue synthetic data can bypass confidentiality and access barriers that have stalled CAMHS research, demonstrating creation and analysis of synthetic data to answer policy-relevant questions. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper is cited in connection with the synthetic data generation approach used, though the abstract does not detail which specific SDV algorithm or tool was run.
preprint-synthetic-child-adolescent-ment.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the SDV software itself was run to generate the CAMHS synthetic data or whether the citation is only background/motivational.

paper-tabby-lm-tabular-2025.summary: Modifies a standard transformer language model for tabular synthesis by replacing selected layers with Gated Mixture-of-Experts blocks that give each column its own parameters, pairs this with a simpler row-serialisation training scheme, and reports quality at or near that of real data across eight tables and one nested JSON dataset. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE representatives among the non-language-model baselines, carried as rows through the machine-learning-efficacy, discrimination and distance-to-closest-record tables.

preprint-balancing-optimality-diversity-.summary: This paper proposes generative curation, a decision-theoretic framework for algorithms that produce a diverse portfolio of quantitatively strong recommendations for a human decision-maker to choose from, formalizing a trade-off between optimality and qualitative diversity via a Gaussian-process model. It develops neural generative and sequential optimization implementations and validates them on synthetic experiments and a police redistricting case study. CTGAN is cited only in passing, in the introduction's list of areas where generative models have been applied (synthetic data generation), with no use of the SDV library or its methods in the work itself.

preprint-predictive-mimicker-mechanical-.summary: This preprint develops a machine-learning model to predict the mechanical properties of eco-efficient bricks made with waste glass, aiming to reduce the need for costly physical testing in sustainable construction material design. No abstract or full text was available to determine how the model or dataset was built. The paper cites the TGAN (2018) paper from the SDV family, apparently only as a reference.
preprint-predictive-mimicker-mechanical-.needs: Only metadata was available; no abstract or citing sentence text to confirm whether TGAN was run, discussed, or merely listed in references.

preprint-fair-supervised-learning-simple.summary: This paper proposes a fairness-penalty framework for supervised learning that uses a simple random sampler of sensitive attributes to enforce independence, separation, or sufficiency notions of fairness, and gives theoretical guarantees plus empirical benchmark comparisons. CTGAN is not run; it is cited twice in passing as an example of a generative model used elsewhere for synthesizing fair datasets and as an illustration of the training difficulty of GANs on mixed categorical/continuous sensitive attributes.

preprint-constrained-time-series-generat.summary: This paper addresses generating synthetic time series that are both statistically realistic and satisfy externally imposed numerical constraints, proposing a constrained-optimization framework and a guided diffusion model called 'GuidedDiffTime' that avoids costly retraining or rejection sampling when constraints change. It evaluates the approach on financial and energy time-series datasets, showing improved realism and constraint satisfaction with reduced computational cost. The SDV paper is cited only in passing as an example of the reject-and-resample approach to constraint enforcement, with no SDV code run.

paper-synthetic-population-india-2022.summary: Builds a synthetic population for India at several administrative levels by combining census, IHDS-II, NSS and gridded population sources, assigning individuals to households and households to administrative units so that the result can seed agent-based simulation. CTGAN is one of the generators trialled for producing the base population and is reported as rejected in favour of iterative proportional updating, on the ground that IPU can match individual-level and household-level characteristics simultaneously while CTGAN cannot.

preprint-faux-testing-individual-fairnes.summary: This paper proposes fAux, a method for testing individual fairness in machine learning models by comparing gradients of a target model to those of an auxiliary model that predicts a protected variable from the input features. For tabular datasets, the authors adopt a preprocessing strategy similar to CTGAN's, modeling each feature with a Gaussian Mixture Model, but implement this themselves rather than running the CTGAN library. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique is cited and its idea adapted in the authors' own preprocessing pipeline, not executed as a generator.

preprint-ctab-gan-effective-table-2021.summary: This paper proposes CTAB-GAN, a conditional GAN-based tabular data synthesizer that models mixed continuous/categorical variables and addresses imbalanced and long-tailed distributions via a classifier loss, information loss, and an extended conditional vector. It is evaluated against four state-of-the-art tabular GAN baselines (CTGAN, TableGAN, CWGAN, MedGAN) on five ML datasets for statistical similarity and ML utility. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional-vector design are explicitly adopted as inspiration, and CTGAN itself is reimplemented from its published description (not the sdv-dev library) to serve as the closest-performing comparison baseline.
preprint-ctab-gan-effective-table-2021.needs: Metadata lists the cited SDV paper as TGAN (2018), but the body text clearly discusses and reimplements CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional vector design as a baseline; likely a citation mismatch between TGAN and CTGAN in the reference list.

preprint-synthetic-observational-health-.summary: A systematic review of published GAN-based methods for generating synthetic observational health data (electronic health records), surveying algorithms, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility practices across the field. The review discusses CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach to tabular data and notes that HealthGAN adapted a data-transformation method from the Synthetic Data Vault; a glossary entry describes SDV as a Gaussian-copula-based generative model for relational databases. Neither CTGAN nor SDV is run by the authors themselves; both are discussed as prior work within the surveyed literature.

repo-vector-diffusion-models.summary: Vector Institute bootcamp material on diffusion models for tabular and time-series data, with worked single-table and multi-table synthesis pipelines. SDV is the measuring instrument throughout: `gen_multi_report.py` imports `evaluate_quality` from both `sdv.evaluation.single_table` and `sdv.evaluation.multi_table`, the pipelines build `MultiTableMetadata` and `SingleTableMetadata`, and density and detection scores come from SDMetrics' `QualityReport` and `LogisticDetection`, with `sdv==1.11.0` pinned. SDV's metadata and evaluation layers are run to score models it did not produce.

repo-synthetic-data-workshop.summary: Workshop material on building synthetic data generation with a range of tools, extending into how to serve the result as a microservice. SDV is the machine-learning half of it: the intro notebook opens with `sdv.lite.SingleTablePreset`, `sdv.datasets.demo.download_demo` and the `sdv.evaluation.single_table` trio of `get_column_plot`, `evaluate_quality` and `run_diagnostic`, and the engineering notebook fits a `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` over a `SingleTableMetadata`. SDV's preset, synthesizer and evaluation module are run as the workshop's modelling track.
